old: Its ultimate root names a god of hot, foaming springs.
It's named after a French royal house, by way of a county in Kentucky.
Some also trace it to a New Orleans street named for that same dynasty.
clues: This liquor has a name that traces back, through a French royal dynasty, to a Celtic god of bubbling hot springs.
A distinctly American whiskey, made mostly from corn and aged in new charred oak barrels, sweeter than Scotch or rye. It is named for a Kentucky county.
The classic base of a mint julep or Old Fashioned, it shares its name with New Orleans' famous French Quarter party street, which possibly helped name it.
